bugs.text: Every one of the 40 enemies fires straight down from the formation on an independent 170-420 frame timer (plus 0.4%/frame while entering), giving a constant rain of roughly 8 bullets per second across the formation's width. The play-test screenshots show ~25 enemy bullets on screen at 5 s, one reserve already gone at 8 s and game over (score 80) by 15 s; the second and third games also ended within 30 s. Dives and the tractor beam are rarely reached before all three ships are gone.

'PRESS ENTER TO START' is drawn only when frameCount is an exact multiple of 60 (one frame per second), so the title effectively never shows the start prompt; confirmed by all three title screenshots.
Boss Galaga shot while diving with two escorts scores 1200 (400 * (1 + 2)), not 1600 as the spec and the title's own score table say.
Challenging-stage wave bonuses (1000) and the PERFECT 10000 are accumulated in challengeBonus and displayed, but never added to the score.

A freed captured fighter only docks if it is within 4 px of the player's side slot at the instant it reaches the player's y; its x lags a moving player by ~18 px, so a moving player makes it overshoot, fly off the bottom and stay in freedShips forever. The rescue is lost.
Capture has no pull-up animation: the ship explodes with a player-death explosion and the red captive appears instantly above the boss.
Tractor-beam dives are impossible on stage 1 (stage > 1 gate), so the signature mechanic cannot appear until the second stage.
Losing the last ship switches to gameOver immediately and renderGameOver draws no entities, so the final death explosion is never shown.
A challenge enemy destroyed by ramming the player counts as a hit (challengeHits++) toward NUMBER OF HITS and PERFECT, but as 'gone' for the wave bonus.
Six Zako sprite rows are 15 characters wide instead of 16, so the right edge of the sprite is clipped by a pixel in both frames.
Holding Space auto-fires every step a slot is free; combined with the two-shot cap it is tolerable but not the arcade's one shot per press.

summary: The code is cleanly organised: a proper fixed-step loop, state/update/render kept apart, a hand-made bitmap font, pixel sprites, synthesized audio, and almost every spec feature has real, reachable code behind it, including the two-hit Boss, escort dives, the tractor beam, capture, rescue-to-dual-fighter, captive fire, challenging stages, denomination flags, READY respawn and localStorage high score. Fidelity is where it falls down. The enemy sprites are coloured diamonds rather than a bee, a butterfly and a boss, the Goei/Boss 'wing flap' is a one-pixel shift, the capture has no pull-up, and the formation fires straight down from every slot, which turns Galaga's rhythm of dives into a bullet hell that ended each of the play-test's games in well under thirty seconds before a dive or beam was ever seen. Add a start prompt that is invisible 59 frames in 60, a 1200-instead-of-1600 Boss payout, challenge bonuses that are shown but never scored, and a rescue dock that misses a moving player, and the result reads as a competent, well-structured clone whose balance and polish were never play-tested.
